task.description:
Final gate on ADHOC-20260821-002, after rework iteration 2. Your step-04 re-gate confirmed G1..G7 closed and FAILed on G8 alone; ORCH folded in G9, G10 and G11 (G10 against your own non-gating ruling — reasoning in step-05's task description, and you should feel free to disagree with it). DOC-UPDATER reports all four closed in commit 39e8d27. Review `git show 39e8d27`.

Rework budget stands at 2 of 3. That is context for your verdict, not pressure on it: if something is genuinely not closed, FAIL it and say so — the cost of a third iteration is one agent turn, and the cost of a wrong rule in this corpus is every future run. But do not manufacture a finding to justify a third pass either. If this is done, say it is done.

WHAT TO CHECK, in priority order:

  1. **G8 closure, and specifically whether the new template can still be satisfied wrongly.** The old defect was that the template PRESCRIBED a bare `PASS` next to a non-zero failure count. Check the replacement actually removes that affordance rather than relocating it: is there any way to complete the `mix test` line that reads as a clean verdict without stating counts and an attribution route? DOC-UPDATER's own residual-risk admission is that an agent can still write numbers it did not measure — agreed and unavoidable, do not treat that as the gap. The gap to test for is whether the TEMPLATE still offers a compliant-looking way out.

  2. **The sibling-line judgements.** DOC-UPDATER amended SECURITY-REVIEWER's line, and deliberately LEFT BARE both `mix compile --warnings-as-errors: PASS` (argued: genuinely zero-tolerance, so the label is a complete statement) and `RELEASE-VALIDATOR: PASS` (argued: its subject is already listed two lines above in the same body). Rule on both. A wrong call here reintroduces G8's shape on a different line, and 'we checked the siblings' is the kind of claim that is easy to assert and easy to get wrong.

  3. **No regression across all three commits.** This pass has 9 deletions, 7 of them a whole-paragraph rewrite in core-directives. Verify independently that R1's three routes, R4's carve-out and its 'including your own measurement' clause, R5's probe, the 13-15 measurement, the PinRebindTest and 17/24/11 examples, G3's step-5d block and Precondition, and G4's reciprocal pointers all survive. The cumulative view is `git diff b13a523~1..HEAD` over the affected files.

  4. **G9's empty-set closure actually binds.** The producer role file now requires reporting at least one mutant for the non-existence case. Check that the validator's mandate and the producer's obligation now refer to the same thing, and that neither can be satisfied while the other is not.

  5. **G10 and G11.** G10 you ruled non-gating; confirm the fix is correct and did not break the 'No Issue Left Local-Only' principle it sits inside. G11 is readability — confirm no meaning changed.

Do NOT rewrite the docs. PASS or FAIL. If PASS, state explicitly that the five rules are in force and that nothing further is required before ORCH commits and pushes — ORCH will not push without that.
acceptance_criteria: G8 assessed for whether the template still offers a compliant-looking way to avoid stating counts and an attribution route, distinct from the unavoidable risk of an agent writing unmeasured numbers
An explicit ruling on each of the three sibling-line judgements (SECURITY-REVIEWER amended; compile and RELEASE-VALIDATOR left bare), agreeing or not, with reasoning
G9, G10, G11 each given a closed/not-closed verdict re-derived from the files
G9 specifically checked for whether the producer's obligation and the validator's mandate now bind to the same object and cannot be satisfied independently
No-regression verified across all three commits by naming the specific surviving elements listed in the task description, with any casualty named
All 9 deletions in this pass accounted for
PASS or FAIL. If PASS, an explicit statement that the five rules are in force and nothing further is required before commit and push
No file outside handoffs/ is modified by this step

result.summary:
PASS. G8, G9, G10 and G11 are all CLOSED, re-derived from the current files rather than from step-05's report. G1-G7 remain closed (re-derived at step 04; this iteration is additive and touches none of them). The five rules R1-R5 are in force. Nothing further is required before ORCH commits and pushes.

ITEM 1 -- G8: CLOSED. THE TEMPLATE NO LONGER OFFERS A COMPLIANT-LOOKING WAY OUT. GIT_MERGE.md lines 178-180 now read `- mix test: <passed> passed, <N> failed, 0 attributable to this branch / (attribution route <1|2|3>: <one clause naming the evidence>; recorded in handoffs/<run-id>/)`. I tested this the way the task asked -- by trying to complete the line as a clean verdict without counts and without a route -- and enumerated every completion an agent actually has. (a) WRITE A VERDICT TOKEN: impossible, there is no slot for one; `PASS` is not a grammatical completion of `<passed> passed, <N> failed` and the warning at 189-201 forbids it by name and by rule ('a bare PASS next to a non-zero failure count is a red pipeline labelled OK without its source'). (b) FILL IT CORRECTLY: the intended path, and cheapest -- both values already exist at step 5d. (c) LEAVE THE PLACEHOLDERS: publishes literal `<passed>`/`<1|2|3>` angle brackets in the PR body, conspicuous rather than plausible. (d) TAKE THE ZERO BRANCH -- the one real candidate, since the warning says 'If `<N>` is 0, write `0 failed` and drop the parenthetical', which does yield a short clean-looking line. That is NOT an affordance, and the distinction is the one the task drew: `0 failed` is a FACTUAL CLAIM about a measurement, not a VERDICT LABEL. The old `PASS` was a label that stayed formally true beside 14 failures once G3 redefined green, which is exactly why it was a way out; `0 failed` beside 14 failures is simply false. Reaching (d) dishonestly requires writing a number the agent did not measure -- DOC-UPDATER's conceded residual, unpreventable by any template, and correctly excluded from this item. CONCLUSION: after the fix there is no completion of the line that is BOTH true given a non-zero run AND free of counts and an attribution route. The affordance is removed, not relocated. Two supporting checks: the literal `0 attributable to this branch` is hard-coded rather than slotted, which is right -- any other value means step 5d should have blocked the merge; and the warning is placed immediately after the `gh pr create` command and outside the body string, so it cannot be pasted into a PR by accident.

OBSERVATION (non-gating, no change required): the parenthetical affords ONE route and ONE clause, so a run whose N failures split across routes 1 and 2 has no templated shape for that. In practice `route 1|2` or `routes 1 and 2` fits the slot, the per-failure detail is where the line already says it is (`recorded in handoffs/<run-id>/`), and the item's requirement -- that a PR-only reader can see failures occurred and on what basis they were cleared -- is met. Recorded so it is not rediscovered as a defect; I do not ask for it to be changed.

ITEM 2 -- THE THREE SIBLING-LINE JUDGEMENTS. I AGREE WITH ALL THREE, but I reach the third on a different and stronger reason than DOC-UPDATER gave, and that difference is worth recording.

  (a) `SECURITY-REVIEWER: PASS | out of scope (<one clause: why no tenant-data path>)` -- AMENDING IT WAS CORRECT. 'Out of scope' is a judgement made off-PR that a PR-only reader cannot distinguish from 'never looked at', which is G8's shape exactly. Note the amendment is better targeted than it looks: the reason slot attaches to the `out of scope` branch specifically (its prompt text is 'why no tenant-data path'), not to `PASS`. That is right -- `PASS` means the gate RAN and has a handoff artefact behind it, whereas `out of scope` means it did not run, and only the second needs its source carried. No change wanted.

  (b) `mix compile --warnings-as-errors: PASS` -- LEAVING IT BARE WAS CORRECT, and I confirmed the premise mechanically rather than accepting it. The argument only holds if nothing in the doc set redefines compile-green the way G3 redefined test-green. `grep -rn 'warnings-as-errors' docs/ .claude/ CLAUDE.md` returns six hits (GIT_MERGE.md 25, 143, 177, 198; WF-02 174, 193) and NONE carries a tolerance, a standing-warning set, or a carve-out; WF-02 line 193's acceptance criterion is the flat `exits 0`. With zero tolerance and no redefinition, `PASS` on that line is a complete statement, not a label standing in for an off-PR justification. G8's shape is not present. No change wanted.

  (c) `RELEASE-VALIDATOR: PASS` -- LEAVING IT BARE IS THE RIGHT CALL, BUT DOC-UPDATER'S REASON IS NOT THE ONE THAT SAVES IT, and had the reason been the whole story I would have ruled the other way. Its stated reason is that the verdict's subject is 'already listed two lines above in the same body'. That is loose on the fact (the `## Requirements` list is a section above, not two lines) and, more importantly, it answers the wrong question: G8 was never about a missing SUBJECT, it was about a missing SOURCE for an OK label on a red run. And this line is genuinely exposed to that: `.claude/agents/release-validator.md` line 29 requires RELEASE-VALIDATOR to 're-run `mix test` yourself', so its PASS is a verdict rendered over the same suite carrying the same standing 13-15 failures, resting on the same structural attribution -- a second measurement, not the one reported on the `mix test` line. THE REASON IT SURVIVES: the specific harm G8 targets is a reader forming a false impression that the pipeline was clean. After the G8 fix, the same PR body states `<N> failed` three lines above, so no reader of `RELEASE-VALIDATOR: PASS` can be misled about the suite's redness -- the disclosure is already in the artefact, which is precisely the property the PR body was missing before. And unlike `out of scope`, `PASS` here always means the gate ran and produced a handoff. So: leave it bare, on that basis. Recording the reason matters because the weak version of it ('the subject is nearby') would license leaving any future validator line bare, including one added to a body that no longer carries a count.

ITEM 3 -- NO REGRESSION ACROSS ALL THREE COMMITS. Verified independently by reading the current files, not the diffs. Every element named in the task survives: R1's THREE ROUTES (core-directives 322-330, routes 1 and 2 with their `; or` terminators, route 3 with 'evidenced by a measurement of the actual mechanism, never by assertion') plus its anti-escape-hatch sentence at 347-349 and the 'report it as unattributed and file it' residue at 350; R4's CARVE-OUT with the exact clause 'a safety/gate rule is never overridable by anything, INCLUDING YOUR OWN MEASUREMENT' (HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md 54-56, verbatim); R5's PROBE, the out-of-tree fabricated off-pin version file run under a re-derivation (core-directives 119-123); the 13-15 MEASUREMENT (GIT_MERGE.md 30-31); the PINREBINDTEST example with its whitespace-re-wrap-at-513-517 vs failure-at-351 mechanism (core-directives 376-381); the MUTANT COUNTS 17/30, 24/30, 11/30 (WF-03 123-126); G3's STEP-5D BLOCK (GIT_MERGE.md 147-158, including the re-qualified terminator 'If FAIL (i.e. at least one failure is attributable to this branch, or is unattributed)') and its PRECONDITION twin (30-37); G4's RECIPROCAL POINTERS in both directions -- R1 -> Scope boundary at core-directives 316-320, Scope boundary -> R1 at 251-253. NO CASUALTIES. Nothing is weakened, reworded to a weaker force, or orphaned.

DELETION ACCOUNTING -- ALL 9, INDIVIDUALLY. `git show 39e8d27 --numstat` gives 10/0 test-designer.md, 9/7 core-directives.md, 18/2 GIT_MERGE.md (the fourth path is step-05's handoff, 61/0, new file). test-designer.md is PURELY ADDITIVE -- zero deletions, so nothing there can have been lost. GIT_MERGE.md's 2: `- mix test: PASS` and `- SECURITY-REVIEWER: PASS | out of scope`, the two G8 template lines, each replaced in place by a longer form of itself (extracted with `git show ... -U0 | grep '^-' | grep -v '^---'`, since a `^-[^-]` filter silently misses deleted lines that themselves begin with `-`, which both of these do -- worth noting, an accounting that used the naive filter would have found only 7 and declared the numstat wrong). core-directives.md's 7: the entire old Scope-boundary body, one contiguous block, rewritten in place. Line by line -- lines 1-2 carried G4's cross-reference clause, re-added VERBATIM as its own sentence at the end of the paragraph (G11); line 3 carried the 'unrelated, not blocking your acceptance criteria' apposition, re-added and now correctly adjacent to the noun it defines; lines 4-5 carried the `docs/issues/ISS-NNNN.yaml` + `gh` instruction, which is the deletion G10 REQUIRED; line 5 also carried the 'No Issue Left Local-Only' pointer, re-added; lines 6-7 carried 'It becomes its own later run, not an unbounded scope creep on this one', re-added verbatim. NO deletion removes a rule, an incident citation, a measurement, or a worked example. Zero unaccounted.

ITEM 4 -- G9: CLOSED, AND THE TWO OBLIGATIONS NOW BIND TO THE SAME OBJECT. The object is 'at least one mutant, reported in TEST-DESIGNER's handoff, with measured counts'. Producer side, test-designer.md 53-62: for the non-existence case the pre-fix check 'is trivially satisfied and proves nothing', so TEST-DESIGNER MUST mutate the shipped logic and 'report at least one mutant with its measured counts (which tests failed, how many) in your handoff'. Validator side, test-design-validator.md 30-40: MUST 'apply at least one of TEST-DESIGNER's reported mutants to the shipped logic yourself, run the suite, and quote your own measured counts', mandatory, not subject to a cheapness test, not satisfied by reading the reported counts. Same object, same cardinality, from both ends. CAN EITHER BE SATISFIED WHILE THE OTHER IS NOT? Producer satisfied, validator not: the validator would be skipping an unconditional MUST whose only escape clause (the cheapness test) G1 deleted -- a role-file violation, not a hole. Validator satisfied, producer not: impossible in the direction that matters, because with zero reported mutants the validator has an empty set to draw from and cannot produce the measured counts of its own that its MUST requires, so it has no completable outcome except FAIL. The empty set no longer voids the mandate; it converts into a FAIL on both sides. Cross-reference resolves: test-designer.md cites WF-03's subsection by its exact heading, and WF-03 line 105 is `### When the pre-fix failure is "the code under test does not exist"` -- exact match, and the technique is not restated, so there is one home. RESIDUAL, NON-GATING, NO CHANGE ASKED: the explicit sentence naming an empty mutant set as a FAIL lives in the PRODUCER's file, which the validator need not read; step-04's suggestion had also proposed a mirror of it in the validator's file, and ORCH's step-05 scope covered only the producer half. I do not require the mirror, for two reasons -- the inference is forced (an unconditional MUST with an empty subject cannot be reported satisfied), and WF-03 at rank 3, cited by the validator's own file by exact heading, independently states that the non-existence case is satisfied ONLY by recorded mutants. The mandate always has a subject or a FAIL; it never has an N/A.

ITEM 5 -- G10: CLOSED. The `docs/issues/ISS-NNNN.yaml` + `gh` instruction is gone from core-directives 246-253, replaced by 'report the finding to ORCH per `docs/agents/protocols/ISSUE_QUEUE.md`, which is what makes it visible work' plus the explicit 'You do not call the queue or `gh` yourself and you do not choose an issue id; only ORCH allocates ids, and a discovering agent filing directly is what reintroduces the id-collision class that rule exists to prevent.' No id shape survives in the paragraph; it matches G5's WF-02/WF-04 wording and matches ISSUE_QUEUE.md. THE 'NO ISSUE LEFT LOCAL-ONLY' PRINCIPLE IS INTACT -- its principle is 'a defect that lives only in docs/issues/*.yaml and never becomes visible work is invisible to the next run', and the amended text invokes exactly that ('which is what makes it visible work') and keeps the pointer. The fix did not break it. See G12 below for what the fix DID do to that section's procedure, which I record but do not gate on.

G11: CLOSED, no meaning change. Verified word by word against the pre-39e8d27 text: the em-dash pair now brackets only 'unrelated, not blocking your acceptance criteria', restored as the sole apposition defining 'a defect you merely notice'; G4's clause stands as its own final sentence with identical wording and identical bold ('For a test failure, which side of this line it falls on is decided by "Failure Attribution Is Structural, Never By Count-Matching" below, not by judgement'). No nesting, no re-scoping risk, nothing added or dropped. R1's reciprocal pointer back to the Scope boundary still resolves.

SCOPE OF THIS STEP. `git status --porcelain` shows only `handoffs/ADHOC-20260821-002/step-06-reviewer-final.json`. No file outside handoffs/ was modified; I rewrote no doc. I did not write `handoffs/registry.json` or `handoffs/orchestrator.log` (ORCH's). `completed_at` was read from the clock via `date -u`, not from memory. This is a pipeline-doc gate with no requirement in scope, so there is no requirement status to flip and no status-history event to append.

VERDICT: PASS. THE FIVE RULES R1-R5 ARE IN FORCE, and NOTHING FURTHER IS REQUIRED BEFORE ORCH COMMITS AND PUSHES. G12 below is a MINOR follow-up and explicitly does not block the push.

issues.description: G12 -- G10's FIX PUT core-directives.md INTO CONTRADICTION WITH ITSELF, ONE POINTER APART. NON-GATING; DOES NOT BLOCK THE PUSH. The amended Scope boundary (lines 246-250) says the discovering agent reports to ORCH, does NOT call `gh`, and does NOT choose an issue id -- and in the same sentence points the reader to 'No Issue Left Local-Only below'. That section, lines 259-269, still says the opposite in the discovering agent's voice: any newly discovered issue 'gets registered in `docs/issues/` ... AND, if `gh` is authenticated and the `origin` remote is reachable, filed via `gh issue create`', with a fallback instruction to write `github_issue: null` into 'the issue file' -- which presupposes the discovering agent owns one. This is the third and last home of the defect G5 and G10 were both about; b13a523 did not touch it, so the TEXT is pre-existing, but the CONTRADICTION is new: before 39e8d27 the two paragraphs agreed (both wrong), and now they disagree, with the corrected half routing the reader to the uncorrected half. Same file, same precedence rank, so the Instruction Precedence chain cannot arbitrate between them. WHY I AM NOT GATING ON IT, stated so the standard is auditable: it is the identical situation I ruled non-gating at step 04 when I first raised G10 -- `ISSUE_QUEUE.md` is rank 4 and `core-directives.md` is rank 5, so an agent applying precedence correctly still reaches 'report to ORCH, do not file'. The permissive text sits BELOW the strict text, not above it; this is a coherence defect (G11's class), not the precedence INVERSION that made G1 a blocker. Ruling it gating now would apply a stricter standard to the residual than I applied to the original, which ORCH folded in at its own discretion rather than on my gate. The concrete harm is bounded and is bookkeeping, not a false green: a duplicate or colliding issue id, the class recorded in commit 159fe9e as recurring -- not a red run labelled OK. FIX WHEN CONVENIENT (three lines, in a file already open in this run): in 'No Issue Left Local-Only', keep the principle sentence unchanged and replace the procedure so the discovering agent REPORTS the finding to ORCH per ISSUE_QUEUE.md, with ORCH allocating the id and doing the filing; drop the `gh issue create` instruction and the `github_issue: null` fallback from the discovering agent's voice, or re-attribute both to ORCH. ORCH's options, and MY VERDICT DOES NOT DEPEND ON WHICH IT PICKS: (i) fold it into this commit before pushing under ORCHESTRATOR.md 10's sizing rule -- my preference, since the contradiction was created by this pass and it is cheaper to not ship it than to file it; or (ii) report it to the queue per ISSUE_QUEUE.md as its own later run. What it should NOT need is a third rework iteration -- it is not a gap in the four items I was asked to gate, all of which are closed.

result.next_action: ORCH: the gate is GREEN. The five rules R1-R5 are in force and nothing further is required before commit and push -- proceed with the commit of 39e8d27's follow-on artefacts and the push, and with the registry.json / orchestrator.log entries, which are yours and which I did not touch. No third rework iteration is needed; the budget stays at 2 of 3. G12 (MINOR, above) is the one open item: fold its three-line edit into this push under ORCHESTRATOR.md 10's sizing rule if you prefer not to ship a self-contradicting core-directives.md, or report it to the queue per ISSUE_QUEUE.md as its own later run -- either is acceptable and neither changes this PASS. The two non-gating observations recorded in the summary (the single-route parenthetical in the PR template, and the empty-mutant-set FAIL being stated in the producer's file rather than mirrored in the validator's) need no action and are recorded only so a later gate does not rediscover them as defects.
